Creation Ordinances
kree-AY-shun OR-di-nan-ses
noun (creational law)
English “ordinance” from the Latin ordinare, to set in order; the appointments God instituted at creation, before the fall.

📖 Biblical Definition

The creation ordinances are the standing institutions God appointed at the beginning, before sin entered, and which therefore bind all mankind in every age. Three are commonly numbered: marriage, labour with dominion, and the Sabbath. God made man male and female and joined them in marriage, declaring, “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Gen 2:24); He gave the dominion-mandate, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it,” and set the man in the garden “to dress it and to keep it” (Gen 1:28; 2:15); and He hallowed the seventh day, resting from His work and sanctifying it (Gen 2:2-3). These ordinances are not Mosaic and ceremonial but creational and perpetual, woven into the order of the world by the Maker's own hand. They are not abolished by the fall but preserved through it, though now pursued amid thorns and toil. Our Lord confirms marriage as a creation ordinance, appealing past the law of Moses to “the beginning” (Matt 19), and the New Testament establishes the Lord's Day as the Christian Sabbath, the weekly rest fulfilled and renewed in Christ's resurrection. Christ Himself is the last Adam, who keeps the dominion-mandate by subduing all His enemies, who takes the church as His bride in a marriage of which Eden's was the type, and who gives His people the true rest that the Sabbath foreshadowed. The creation ordinances thus order human life under God and find their consummation in the work of the second Adam.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The pre-fall institutions of marriage, labour and dominion, and the Sabbath, ordained at creation and binding on all mankind.

CREATION ORDINANCES, noun (creational law). From the Latin ordinare, to set in order; the appointments God instituted at the beginning.

Standing institutions established before the fall and binding upon all men.

Commonly numbered as marriage, labour with dominion, and the Sabbath rest.

Grounded in the work of the first week: “And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.” (Gen 2:3)

Figuratively, the created framework within which human life is rightly ordered.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 1:28 — "And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth."

Gen 2:3 — "And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made."

Gen 2:15 — "And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it."

Gen 2:24 — "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The creation ordinances are openly assailed by an age that severs marriage, labour, and rest from their created design.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Yet each ordinance is pressed by the spirit of the age—marriage redefined against its created form of one man and one woman, labour resented or worshipped, and rest swallowed by ceaseless toil or idleness. The principle to recover is that these are creational and perpetual, ordained before the fall and binding on all mankind, not arrangements men may renegotiate.

The recovery is to honour the Maker's order from the beginning, as our Lord did when He appealed past Moses to creation itself. Marriage, dominion, and Sabbath are preserved through the fall and find their consummation in Christ the last Adam, who weds His church, subdues every foe, and gives the true rest the seventh day foreshadowed.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The phrase joins the doctrine of creation to the Latin sense of an appointed order.

expand to see more

ordinare (Latin) — to set in order, arrange, appoint.

Hebrew bara' — to create; the act establishing these standing appointments.

Hebrew shabath — to cease or rest; the root of Sabbath.

Hebrew radah — to have dominion, rule; the dominion-mandate.

Hebrew dabaq — to cleave or cling; the bond of one-flesh marriage.

Usage

"Of the three pre-fall institutions of marriage, labour, and the Sabbath."

"Of the perpetual, creational law binding all mankind apart from Moses."

"Of the Lord's Day as the Christian Sabbath fulfilled in Christ's resurrection."
